actions.justification: Mandatory Hour-1 Bundle element: measure serum lactate immediately to risk-stratify and guide resuscitation. Elevated lactate (>2 mmol/L) confirms tissue hypoperfusion; >4 mmol/L mandates aggressive fluid resuscitation.
Mandatory Hour-1 Bundle element: obtain blood cultures BEFORE antibiotics to identify causative organism and guide de-escalation of therapy. Must not delay antibiotic administration.
Mandatory Hour-1 Bundle element: administer empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics immediately after blood cultures are drawn. Every hour of delay in antibiotics increases mortality in septic shock.
MANDATORY per SSC Hour-1 Bundle: administer 30 mL/kg IV crystalloid rapidly for hypotension (BP 85/50, MAP 62). Must be completed within 60 minutes of recognition.

Patient is persistently hypotensive (MAP 62 mmHg, target ≥65 mmHg) with signs of shock. Norepinephrine is first-line vasopressor per SSC guidelines. Should be initiated if hypotension persists during or after fluid resuscitation.

Evaluate for multi-organ dysfunction (altered mental status, SpO2 92%, hypotension suggest potential neurologic, respiratory, and cardiovascular involvement). Guides further management and severity assessment.

Patient is on vasopressors with borderline MAP of 62 mmHg and SpO2 of 92%. Serial vital sign reassessment is critical to evaluate response to norepinephrine and fluid resuscitation, and to determine if additional vasopressors or oxygen support are needed.
Identifying the source of infection (pulmonary, urinary, abdominal, etc.) is essential to guide targeted antibiotic therapy and source control interventions per SSC guidelines.
Basic metabolic panel is needed to evaluate renal function (creatinine, BUN), electrolytes, glucose, and acid-base status as markers of organ dysfunction in septic shock.

Initial lactate was 4.5 mmol/L (>2 mmol/L). SSC guidelines mandate serial lactate measurements to guide resuscitation and assess response to treatment. Remeasuring at ~45 minutes post-arrival is appropriate.

Patient received 30 mL/kg crystalloid and norepinephrine. Reassess perfusion status (MAP, mental status, urine output, skin perfusion) to evaluate response to resuscitation and determine if additional interventions are needed.

Patient is in septic shock on vasopressor support. Arterial line provides continuous blood pressure monitoring, which is essential for titrating norepinephrine and detecting hemodynamic changes in real time.

MAP remains at 62 mmHg (below target of 65 mmHg) despite norepinephrine. SSC guidelines recommend adding vasopressin (up to 0.03 units/min) to norepinephrine to either raise MAP to target or to decrease norepinephrine dosage in refractory septic shock.
Central venous access is needed for reliable vasopressor administration, CVP monitoring, and to facilitate ongoing resuscitation in this patient with septic shock requiring multiple vasopressors.

SpO2 is 92% with RR 24 and confirmed gram-negative bacteremia. Chest X-ray is needed to identify pulmonary source of infection (pneumonia), assess for pulmonary edema from fluid resuscitation, and guide further management.

CBC provides critical information on white blood cell count (infection severity), hemoglobin (anemia contributing to poor oxygen delivery with SpO2 92%), and platelet count (DIC risk in septic shock with gram-negative bacteremia).

Coagulation studies (PT/INR, PTT, fibrinogen) are essential to evaluate for DIC, which is a serious complication of gram-negative septic shock. Lactate of 4.5 and positive blood cultures increase this risk.
Procalcitonin serves as a baseline biomarker for bacterial infection severity and can guide antibiotic de-escalation decisions. Elevated levels expected given confirmed gram-negative bacteremia.

Patient has persistent hypotension (MAP 62, BP 85/50) and elevated lactate (4.5 mmol/L). Additional crystalloid fluid administration is indicated per SSC guidelines to support resuscitation and maintain MAP ≥65 mmHg, even though initial 30mL/kg bolus has been given. Ongoing fluid resuscitation guided by perfusion reassessment is appropriate.

MANDATORY action: Patient remains hypotensive (BP 85/50, MAP 62) despite fluid resuscitation. SSC guidelines require vasopressors to maintain MAP ≥65 mmHg. Although norepinephrine and vasopressin have been started, this mandatory bundle element must be formally completed to ensure adequate vasopressor therapy is documented and titrated.

Patient has septic shock with positive blood cultures (gram-negative), lactate 4.5 mmol/L, altered mental status, and ongoing hemodynamic instability requiring vasopressors and intensive monitoring. ICU admission is indicated per SSC guidelines for ongoing resuscitation and organ support.

violation_events.description: Action start_vasopressor_if_hypotensive performed 35 min after deadline
